title: Astrid and the Cellar
premise: Yara Oyelaran returns to her grandmother's house to bury her twin brother Yemi, whose body was found in the cellar of a house he hadn't visited in years. As she sorts his belongings, she notices the photographs have changed: every image taken in the house now shows an extra wooden chair, and the noises she dismissed for twelve years begin answering her by name. Digging through grandma's letters, Yara learns that in 1974 the family stole a chair from a drowned neighbor's estate—a chair that belongs to something still waiting below. To survive the harvest moon and free Yemi's restless spirit, Yara must choose between the family's code of silence and returning what was taken, even if it means confessing to a crime no living person committed. She carries the chair down on the night of the moon, gives it back, and walks out at dawn—alive, but no longer able to pretend the dead don't keep accounts.
about_author: Sebastian Almeida is the pen name of a former funeral home assistant who writes horror about grief, inheritance, and the things families agree not to say out loud. Their work has appeared in several small-press anthologies exploring West African diaspora folklore.

chapters.title: The Wrong Twin
chapters.summary: Yara arrives at grandma's house to arrange Yemi's burial, numb with guilt over twelve years of estrangement. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hollow grief sharpened by the suspicion that Yemi died somewhere he should never have been.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback interwoven with the present: Yara catalogues every noise from childhood—the dragging above the ceiling, the wet footsteps—and the rationalizations she built. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the comfort of denial beginning to crack.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Sorting photo albums for the funeral slideshow, Yara finds an unfamiliar wooden chair in pictures spanning five decades—including photos taken after the chair was supposedly sold. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: first true dread.

chapters.title: The Funeral Nobody Films
chapters.summary: At the burial, relatives avoid Yara's questions about the cellar; Aunt Bisi warns her to leave before the harvest moon. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: isolation—the family closes ranks around its silence.

chapters.title: What Yemi Kept
chapters.summary: In Yemi's room, Yara finds a notebook of measurements, dates, and one repeated phrase: 'it wants to be sat in.' POV: Yara, with notebook excerpts. Emotional beat: her twin knew, and never told her.

chapters.title: Grandma's Letters
chapters.summary: Locked in grandma's trunk, Yara reads correspondence from 1974 describing the drowning of neighbor Adaeze Okonkwo and the 'borrowed' chair taken from her flooded parlor. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: inherited guilt made concrete.

chapters.title: The Cellar Door Unlocked
chapters.summary: Yara descends for the first time since childhood and finds the chair itself—dustless, warm, facing the stairs as if waiting. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror fused with a terrible sense of being expected.

chapters.title: Bisi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Aunt Bisi confesses the family pact: each generation feeds the chair small offerings—photographs, hair, names—to keep it sleeping. She begs Yara to continue. POV: alternating Yara/Bisi. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Adaeze
chapters.summary: Researching at the county archive, Yara learns Adaeze had a daughter who vanished the same year, and that the drowning may not have been an accident. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins to take shape.

chapters.title: Sitting
chapters.summary: Yara wakes at 3 a.m. to find the chair standing in her bedroom doorway; in the morning, all mirrors show her seated in it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the haunting turns personal—it isn't asking anymore.

chapters.title: The Family Council
chapters.summary: Relatives convene to decide whether Yara must be 'given' like Adaeze's daughter was; cousin Tunde quietly slips her the original deed proving theft. POV: mostly Tunde. Emotional beat: a crack in the wall of loyalty.

chapters.title: Yemi's Voice
chapters.summary: Through the floorboards, Yara hears her twin—not accusing, but pleading: finish what I started. She realizes he came home to return the chair and died trying. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: Nine Days to the Moon
chapters.summary: Yara drafts a plan: restore the chair to the Okonkwo land and speak Adaeze's name aloud, breaking the pact. Bisi sabotages the truck. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: determination hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: The House Fights Back
chapters.summary: Doors relocate, stairs lengthen, the cellar breathes cold air upward; the house itself is the pact's enforcer. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair—escape routes closing.

chapters.title: Tunde's Price
chapters.summary: Tunde reveals he helped Yemi and shows where Yemi fell; he agrees to drive Yara to the Okonkwo parcel but admits the family will hunt them both. POV: Tunde. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, real stakes.

chapters.title: Confession at the Grave
chapters.summary: Yara publicly reads grandma's 1974 letter at the family plot, naming the theft and the drowned woman; half the relatives walk out, half stay listening. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: truth spoken—irreversible now.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: On the final night, the house seals itself; Bisi, desperate to preserve the pact, locks Yara in the cellar with the chair. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: betrayal by blood at the worst hour.

chapters.title: The Chair Remembers
chapters.summary: Trapped below, Yara sits in the chair deliberately and experiences Adaeze's drowning and her daughter's fate from inside the memory. POV: Yara/Adaeze braided. Emotional beat: empathy as weapon—she finally understands what was owed.

chapters.title: Carrying It Up
chapters.summary: Yara lifts the chair—impossibly heavy, screaming wood—and climbs as the house tears itself apart around her; Tunde breaks the cellar door from above. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: agonizing effort, love made physical.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: At the Okonkwo land under the full moon, Yara sets the chair down, speaks both names, and offers her own apology; the ground opens, accepts, and goes quiet. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: climax—debt paid, not erased.

chapters.title: After the Moon Sets
chapters.summary: Dawn: the photographs are ordinary again, the noises gone, and Yemi's presence lifts like fog. Bisi leaves without a word; Tunde stays to help sell the house. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: exhausted peace, grief finally allowed.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Yara finds a child's drawing tucked in grandma's Bible labeled 'Astrid'—Adaeze's daughter's English name—and mails it to the surviving Okonkwo cousins. Some debts are paid; some stories deserve to be told. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—justice outside the law, remembered on purpose.
